title: Subsets modulo small sets: quotient Boolean algebras

based_on.title: A Course in Universal Algebra
based_on.pages: 127–130 (IV §3, Definition 3.1, Theorem 3.5, and Definition 3.6; Millennium Edition, 2012 update)

summary: Ignoring small differences preserves set operations and turns almost containment into an order on classes.
abstract: Adding or deleting finitely many points preserves infinitude and almost disjointness. Identifying subsets of the natural numbers that differ only finitely gives a Boolean algebra: union, intersection, and complement still obey their usual laws on equivalence classes. Finite sets represent zero, almost containment becomes a partial order, and almost disjoint infinite sets represent disjoint nonzero elements. The same construction works for any ideal, a family of sets designated small that contains the empty set and is closed under taking subsets and finite unions.
